source.title: Approximating network dynamics: Some open problems

accepted.question_text: For the class M of continuous-time ODE neuronal-network models discussed in Theorem 2.1 and the class N of discrete-time finite-state neuronal-network models intended to approximate them, formulate a general notion of consistency that captures when N correctly predicts which excitatory neurons fire during successive episodes of the ODE dynamics, and determine which structural features of an ODE system make the existence of such a finite-state approximation possible.

evidence.quote: How should one deﬁne, in general, consistency between an ODE model M and a discrete-time approxima- tion N? And what structural features of ODE systems do, in general, favor the existence of discrete-time ﬁnite-state approximations as in Theorem 2.1?

accepted.question_text: In the synchronous finite-state neuronal-network class N on a digraph D, where each node i has refractory period p_i and firing threshold th_i, determine whether the third phase transition occurs when all thresholds equal a common value th and the mean indegree is approximately th, and obtain precise analogues of the results from Subsection 3.2 beyond the special case p_i = th_i = 1.

evidence.quote: The preprint version [16] contains a number of generalizations of these results to arbitrary refractory periods ⃗ p, and some results about arbitrary ﬁring thresholds. Generally speaking, when ⃗th = (th,th,...,th ), one would expect the third phase transition to occur when the mean indegree is≈th, but precise characterizations along the lines of the results reviewed in Subsection 3.2 remain open research problems at this time.

accepted.question_text: For the same class N of synchronous finite-state neuronal networks, determine the typical dynamics, including attractor behavior, transient behavior, and phase transitions, when the random connectivity is not a single-type Erdős-Rényi digraph but instead a multitype Erdős-Rényi random digraph, a generic scale-free network, or a small-world network.

evidence.quote: It is of interest to study the dynamics of N for other types of random connectiv- ities, such as multitype Erd˝ os-R´ enyi random digraphs, generic scale-free networks, and small-world networks. Research on these questions is currently ongoing [21].

accepted.question_text: For the more biologically detailed neuronal models of [5], in which excitatory and inhibitory neurons have additional calcium currents and more complex interactions and the induced discrete model allows a cell to fire during several consecutive episodes before other neurons take over, prove a rigorous analogue of Theorem 2.1 establishing a mathematically precise form of consistency between the continuous ODE model M and its discrete-time dynamical-system approximation N.
accepted.context_brief: Rigorous consistency for enriched neuronal models

evidence.quote: It is also of interest to study the dynamics of models with updating rules that are similar to, but not identical with, the ones of Deﬁnition 3.1 and may be more bio- logically realistic for certain types of neuronal networks. Results for some modiﬁed updating rules have been reported in [5, 12, 29]. In the models of [5], both the excitatory neurons in E and the inhibitory neurons in I contain additional cal- cium ionic currents and there are more complex interactions among the cells. A reduction of the resulting ODE models M to discrete-time dynamical systems N is given in that paper. In N, a cell can ﬁre for several consecutive episodes before other neurons take over. Simulations show dynamic clustering and suggest some form of consistency between M and N, but no rigorous result along the lines of Theorem 2.1 is currently known for these models.

accepted.question_text: In the Erdős-Rényi random-digraph setting reviewed in Subsection 3.2 for the special case p_i = th_i = 1 and edge probability π(n) = c/n, prove that the critical constant c_crit governing the phase transition identified in Theorem 3.2 is exactly 1.

evidence.quote: Note that Theorem 3.2 only tells us that 1 ≤ ccrit≤ 2, but simulations strongly suggest that ccrit = 1. ... Problem 1. (How) can one prove that ccrit = 1?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists an edge-probability function π(n) for this neuronal-network model such that the transient length τ(n) grows faster than every polynomial in n, or at least linearly as Ω(n).

evidence.quote: Similarly, Theorem 3.3 indicates that at the lower end of the critical window the lengths of transients will scale only sublinearly, which is not exactly what one would expect if the dynamics were truly complex. Problem 2. Does there existπ(n) such thatτ(n) scales faster than any polynomial? Or even just like Ω(n)?

accepted.question_text: For a Boolean system N with synchronous update map f and an ODE conversion M in the class D2, Theorem 4.3 proves consistency when f is monotone-stepping. Find a necessary and sufficient condition on f under which the conclusion of Theorem 4.3 holds.

evidence.quote: Indeed, we know that some additional assumption on f is needed in the Theorem 4.3, but being monotone- stepping is not a necessary one. Problem 3. Find a necessary and suﬃcient condition onf for which the conclusion of Theorem 4.3 holds.

accepted.question_text: Theorem 4.2 proves strong consistency for one-stepping Boolean networks when the sampling times (T_t(x(0))) are chosen from the switching-time set SW(x(0)). Determine whether Theorem 4.2 extends to a larger class of Boolean networks if these sampling times are chosen by a different method.

evidence.quote: With regard to Theorem 4.2 we know that it is the strongest possible one for the deﬁnition of (Tt(⃗ x(0)))t∈N based on SW (⃗ x(0)), but there might be a better way to conceptualize strong consistency. Problem 4. Does Theorem 4.2 generalize to a larger class of Boolean networks N if the sequences (Tt(⃗ x(0)))t∈N are chosen by a diﬀerent method than in [20]?

accepted.question_text: Formulate and prove the broadest possible abstract versions of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, isolating the general bifurcation structure and time-scale-separation mechanisms that are really needed for consistency or strong consistency between Boolean systems and their ODE realizations.

evidence.quote: While the proofs of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 given in [20] rely on the particular details of the intrinsic dynamics of the signature variables, the author of this note believes that they should remain valid for broader classes of ODE models. Problem 5. Formulate and prove versions of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 in an abstract setting that is as general as possible.

accepted.question_text: For versions of the ODE model class D2 in which robustness is produced by feedback loops among the slower signaling variables and those feedback loops are random rather than fixed, develop appropriate notions of consistency and determine whether consistency becomes a generic property under suitable distributions of such random feedback architectures.

evidence.quote: Therefore one might expect that some version of con- sistency becomes a generic property when these feedback loops of the signaling variables are drawn from a suitable distribution. This brings us round circle to dynamics on networks with random connectivities and to our last problem: Problem 6. Explore notions of consistency for versions of the class D2 that incor- porates random feedback loops.
